summary: Part II of Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration: the compact endgame of Caraiani–Scholze (Ann. of Math. 2017). Layer IG.8 fixes the compact unitary PEL data of Cases 1 (Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties) and 2 (quasi-split at finite places, F⁺ ≠ ℚ), their smooth proper integral models, the local datum at an auxiliary prime split in the imaginary quadratic field 𝒦 with the embedding sets S_i, the Hecke algebra 𝕋^S with its Hecke polynomials, the dual ideal 𝔪^∨, Hecke-equivariant Poincaré duality, and the auxiliary-prime condition with its existence. Layer IG.9 proves Theorem 5.5.7 for Case 2 from the stable Igusa trace identity, the Newton reduction lemma and the spectral expansion; Layer IG.10 proves Corollaries 5.6.2–5.6.3 for Case 1 through the stable Lefschetz identity for the proper Shimura variety; Layer IG.11 assembles Hochschild–Serre to perfectoid level, the Leray reduction to Igusa varieties and minimal-stratum concentration into Theorem 6.3.1, Theorem 1.1 and the integral and twisted-coefficient forms. The Igusa geometry, the period fibres and the perversity are the parent's; the trace formulas are EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison's; the Galois representations are AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII's. Two gaps are recorded: Case 1 base change and Galois assembly (sourceIssues E1), and Case 2 auxiliary-character finite avoidance. The end-theorem chains remain conditional on the recorded Case 1 base-change/assembly gap and Case 2 auxiliary-character avoidance gap; coefficient variants require an admissible trivializing level.

nodes.title: Compact unitary PEL data of Caraiani–Scholze (Cases 1 and 2)
nodes.statement:
Let F⁺ be a totally real field, 𝒦 an imaginary quadratic field and F = F⁺·𝒦 their compositum, a CM field with complex conjugation c. A compact unitary PEL datum of Caraiani–Scholze type is a rational PEL datum (B, *, V, ⟨·,·⟩, h) of type (A) whose similitude group G over ℚ satisfies one of the following.
Case 1 (Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties). B is a central division algebra over F of degree n, * is an involution of the second kind (it restricts to c on F), and V ≅ B is the simple left B-module.
Case 2. B = F, * = c, V is an F-vector space of dimension n with an alternating form ⟨·,·⟩ hermitian for c, F⁺ ≠ ℚ, G is quasi-split at every finite place, and every rational prime ramified in F lies in Spl_{F/F⁺}, the set of rational primes q such that every place of F⁺ above q splits in F.
In both cases one assumes the Shimura varieties are compact: G^ad is anisotropic over ℚ. The datum fixes: the signatures (p_τ, q_τ) of G_ℝ at each embedding τ : F ↪ ℂ, with p_τ + q_τ = n and (p_{τc}, q_{τc}) = (q_τ, p_τ); the Hodge cocharacter μ and the reflex field E ⊂ ℂ; a finite set S of rational primes such that F and G are unramified outside S (in Case 2 with S ⊂ Spl_{F/F⁺}); and a sufficiently small compact open K = K_S·K^S ⊂ G(𝔸_f) with K^S a product of hyperspecial maximal compact subgroups K_q ⊂ G(ℚ_q). S_K denotes the PEL moduli problem over E, which is the disjoint union over a ∈ ker¹(ℚ, G) of Shimura varieties Sh_{K^{(a)}}(G^{(a)}, X^{(a)}), with G^{(a)} locally isomorphic to G and levels transported through fixed finite-local identifications, and d := dim S_K = Σ_{τ∈Φ} p_τq_τ for any CM type Φ of F; equivalently d = ⟨2ρ, μ⟩.
hypotheses: F = F⁺·𝒦 with F⁺ totally real and 𝒦 imaginary quadratic; the field 𝒦 is part of the datum.
Case 1: B a central division algebra over F with an involution of the second kind, V ≅ B.
Case 2: B = F, F⁺ ≠ ℚ, G quasi-split at all finite places, ramified primes of F in Spl_{F/F⁺}, S ⊂ Spl_{F/F⁺}.
Compactness: G^ad anisotropic over ℚ (automatic in Case 1).
K = K_S K^S sufficiently small (neat), K^S hyperspecial.
proofSteps: Take the rational PEL datum, its similitude group and its signatures from PELModuli M0 (PELModuli:M0/rational-pel-datum, PELModuli:M0/similitude-group, PELModuli:M0/signatures); for Case 2 the unitary PEL data with prescribed signatures are PELModuli:M5/unitary-pel-datum.
The involution of the second kind gives type (A) in Kottwitz's classification (PELModuli:M0/albert-types; the page reference of CS17 p. 730 is corrected to [Kot92b] in PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E63).

The moduli problem S_K and its decomposition over ker¹(ℚ, G) into the Shimura varieties of the corresponding locally isomorphic inner forms are PELModuli:M3/ker1-classification and PELModuli:M4/canonical-model-identification; the dimension formula is PELModuli:M2/kodaira-spencer-dimension.
Record the two cases as two constructors of one structure, so that every statement of Layers IG.9–IG.11 names the case it uses.
acceptance: In Case 2 with n = 1 the group G is a torus, S_K is finite étale over E and d = 0.
For the Harris–Taylor signature ((1, n−1) at one τ₀ ∈ Φ and (0, n) at the other τ ∈ Φ) one has d = n − 1.
Case 2 with F⁺ = ℚ is excluded: then F = 𝒦 and the trace-formula input of Layer IG.9 is not available.

nodes.title: Smooth proper integral models of compact unitary Shimura varieties at good primes
nodes.statement: Let (B, *, V, ⟨·,·⟩, h) be a compact unitary datum (Case 1 or 2) and p a prime outside S, so that F and G are unramified at p (in Case 1, B is split at every place of F above p), and let K = K_pK^p with K_p hyperspecial and K^p neat. For a prime 𝔭 | p of E the PEL moduli problem gives a scheme 𝒮_K over O_{E,𝔭} which is smooth and proper of relative dimension d, with generic fibre S_K ⊗_E E_𝔭; the prime-to-p Hecke correspondences extend to finite étale correspondences of the 𝒮_K. In particular every compact unitary datum satisfies the hypothesis 'S_{K^pK_p} proper over O_{E,𝔭}' of the compact fibre theorem.
hypotheses: p ∉ S; K_p hyperspecial; K^p neat.
Case 1 or Case 2 with G^ad anisotropic over ℚ.
proofSteps: Representability and smoothness of the PEL moduli problem at a good prime: PELModuli:M2/representability; relative dimension d from PELModuli:M2/kodaira-spencer-dimension.
Case 1: End_B(V) = B^op is a division algebra, so the moduli problem is proper by PELModuli:M2/properness-when-division.

Case 2: the boundary of the smooth toroidal compactification of ShimuraCompactifications:C5/integral-toroidal-space is indexed by cusp labels (ShimuraCompactifications:C1/cusp-label), which come from rational parabolic subgroups of G; G^ad anisotropic means there are none, so the toroidal compactification equals the moduli problem and the latter is proper (valuative properness of the toroidal compactification).

Representability initially gives a smooth algebraic space. Choose a projective admissible fan in ShimuraCompactifications:C5/integral-toroidal-space for either case; its projective toroidal compactification is a scheme. Anisotropy leaves no rational cusp labels, so it equals the moduli space. This supplies the scheme assertion as well as properness, without strengthening PELModuli:M2/representability.
Prime-to-p Hecke correspondences: level change and Hecke action PELModuli:M1/hecke-action and finite étaleness of level-forgetting maps PELModuli:M6/level-forgetting-maps.
acceptance: n = 1 (Case 2): 𝒮_K is finite étale over O_{E,𝔭}.
A Case 2 datum with G^ad isotropic (not allowed here) has nonempty boundary and its moduli problem is not proper.

nodes.title: The local datum at an auxiliary prime split in 𝒦 and the sets S_i
nodes.statement:
Let p ∉ S be a rational prime split in 𝒦, p = u·u^c, and let 𝔭_1, …, 𝔭_m be the primes of F above u (so pO_F = ∏_i 𝔭_i𝔭_i^c and the 𝔭_i correspond to the primes of F⁺ above p). Fix a prime 𝔭 | p of E and an isomorphism ι_p : ℚ̄_p ≅ ℂ compatible with E ↪ ℂ and E ↪ E_𝔭 ↪ ℚ̄_p. Then:
(1) G_{ℚ_p} ≅ ∏_{i=1}^m Res_{F_{𝔭_i}/ℚ_p} GL_n × 𝔾_m, the last factor being the similitude factor, through the projection V ⊗ ℚ_p → ⊕_i V ⊗_F F_{𝔭_i} (in Case 1 after a choice of splitting of B ⊗_F F_{𝔭_i}); hence G(ℚ_p) ≅ ∏_i GL_n(F_{𝔭_i}) × ℚ_p^× and every irreducible π_p of G(ℚ_p) is ⊗_i π_{𝔭_i} ⊗ π_0.
(2) S_i := {τ : F ↪ ℂ | ι_p^{−1} ∘ τ : F ↪ ℚ̄_p induces 𝔭_i}; the S_i are pairwise disjoint and their union is the set of embeddings inducing a prime above u.
(3) μ = ((μ_i)_i, μ_0) with μ_i = (μ_{i,τ})_{τ∈S_i} and μ_{i,τ}(t) = diag(t^{(p_τ)}, 1^{(q_τ)}) in GL_n.
(4) B(G, μ^{−1}) = ∏_i B(G_i, μ_i^{−1}) with G_i = Res_{F_{𝔭_i}/ℚ_p} GL_n, and for b = ((b_i), b_0) one has J_b ≅ ∏_i J_{b_i} × 𝔾_m.
(5) If S_i contains exactly one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0, let c_i be the number of τ′ ∈ S_i with signature (n, 0); Shapiro's bijection and multiplication by the central element p^{c_i} identify B(G_i, μ_i^{−1}) with B(GL_n/F_{𝔭_i}, μ_{i,τ}^{−1}), preserving J_b up to restriction of scalars and the μ-ordinary class. If S_i contains no such τ, μ_i is central and B(G_i, μ_i^{−1}) is a single point.
hypotheses: p ∉ S, p split in 𝒦; in Case 1, B split above p (automatic for p ∉ S).
ι_p compatible with the chosen 𝔭 | p of E.
proofSteps: The decomposition of G_{ℚ_p} follows from F ⊗ ℚ_p = ∏_i (F_{𝔭_i} × F_{𝔭_i^c}) and the hermitian pairing identifying the 𝔭_i^c-part with the dual of the 𝔭_i-part (PELModuli:M0/unramified-tau-decomposition; the local datum is IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.0/unramified-local-pel-datum).
The sets S_i are defined with ι_p^{−1} ∘ τ; CS17 prints ι_p ∘ τ, which is undefined (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E86).
Products and unramified restriction of scalars in B(G): BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1/product-and-unramified-norm, with J_b^G ≅ Res J_{Nm(b)}^H.

The central correction p^{c_i} is PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E87: the Shapiro bound is the sum of the components μ_{i,τ′} over τ′ ∈ S_i, i.e. μ_{i,τ} + c_i·z with z(t) = t·I_n; multiplication by the central Frobenius-fixed p^{c_i} is a bijection of Kottwitz sets preserving J_b and the maximal element.
acceptance: If p splits completely in F then every S_i is a singleton and m = [F⁺:ℚ].
For n = 1 every B(G_i, μ_i^{−1}) is a point.

nodes.title: The Hecke algebra 𝕋^S, the operators T_{i,v} and the Hecke polynomial
nodes.statement: Let Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} be the set of rational primes split in 𝒦 and ℓ a prime. The abstract Hecke algebra is 𝕋^S := ⊗'_{q ∈ Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ})} ℤ[G(ℚ_q)//K_q], the restricted tensor product of the spherical Hecke rings. For q ∈ Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) and a place v of F above q, G(ℚ_q) = ∏_w GL_n(F_w) × ℚ_q^× with w over the place of 𝒦 below v; T_{i,v} ∈ ℤ[G(ℚ_q)//K_q] (0 ≤ i ≤ n) is the characteristic function of GL_n(O_{F_v})·diag(ϖ_v^{(i)}, 1^{(n−i)})·GL_n(O_{F_v}) × ∏_{w≠v} GL_n(O_{F_w}) × ℤ_q^×, with i entries ϖ_v, and T_{n,v} is invertible. The Hecke polynomial at v is P_v(X) = Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2} T_{i,v} X^{n−i} ∈ 𝕋^S[X], q_v = |O_F/𝔭_v|. 𝕋^S acts on H^i(S_{K,Ē}, Λ) for every coefficient ring Λ through the Hecke correspondences, and its subalgebra 𝕋^{S∪{p}} acts on the cohomology of Igusa varieties through G(𝔸_f^p); the p-factor of 𝕋^S does not act through this prime-to-p action. A maximal ideal 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^S has finite residue field 𝕋^S/𝔪 of characteristic ℓ when it is in the support of H^*(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ).
hypotheses: S as in the datum; ℓ any prime; v above q ∈ Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}).
proofSteps: The spherical Hecke ring at q is the double-coset ring of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.1/hecke-ring-comparison (Mathlib's HeckeRing with Tau Ceti's ring structure HeckeCosetModule.instRingHeckeRing).

At q split in 𝒦 the group G(ℚ_q) is a product of general linear groups and a similitude factor; T_{i,v} is the GL_n(F_v) generator of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.4/gln-generators placed in the v-factor; T_{n,v} is the class of the central element ϖ_v and is invertible.
CS17 prints ℤ_p^× and ℚ_p^× in the definition of T_{i,v}; the similitude factor at q is ℤ_q^× ⊂ ℚ_q^× (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E12).
Galois-type maximal ideals and their residual representations follow AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.7/hecke-maximal-ideal-of-galois-type with this polynomial and geometric Frobenius.
acceptance: For n = 1, T_{1,v} is the class of ϖ_v ∈ F_v^× and P_v(X) = X − T_{1,v}.

nodes.title: The dual ideal 𝔪^∨ and its Galois representation
nodes.statement: Let ι be the involution of 𝕋^S induced by [K_qgK_q] ↦ [K_qg^{−1}K_q] (an anti-involution of a commutative ring, hence an involution) and 𝔪^∨ := ι(𝔪) for a maximal ideal 𝔪. Then (1) ι(T_{i,v}) = T_{n,v}^{−1}T_{n−i,v}; (2) if λ_1, …, λ_n are the roots of P_v modulo 𝔪 (in 𝔽̄_ℓ), the roots of P_v modulo 𝔪^∨ are q_v^{n−1}λ_1^{−1}, …, q_v^{n−1}λ_n^{−1}; (3) if 𝔪 is of Galois type with semisimple ρ_𝔪 : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(𝔽̄_ℓ) unramified outside the places above S ∪ {ℓ}, then 𝔪^∨ is of Galois type with ρ_{𝔪^∨} ≅ ρ_𝔪^∨ ⊗ ε̄^{1−n} (ε̄ the mod ℓ cyclotomic character, geometric Frobenius conventions of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.0); (4) for a place 𝔭_i of F not above S ∪ {ℓ}, ρ_𝔪 is unramified and decomposed generic at 𝔭_i if and only if ρ_{𝔪^∨} is; hence (p, 𝔭) satisfies the auxiliary-prime condition for 𝔪 if and only if it does for 𝔪^∨.
hypotheses: 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^S maximal with finite residue field; (3)–(4) for Galois-type 𝔪.
proofSteps: (1): the double coset of diag(ϖ_v^{(i)}, 1^{(n−i)})^{−1} equals ϖ_v^{−1}·GL_n(O)diag(1^{(i)}, ϖ_v^{(n−i)})GL_n(O), and multiplication by the central double coset T_{n,v}^{−1} is a single double coset; the other factors are unchanged.
(2): T_{i,v} ≡ q_v^{−i(i−1)/2}e_i(λ) mod 𝔪; substituting (1) gives coefficients (−1)^i q_v^{i(n−1)} e_i(λ^{−1}) for 𝔪^∨, i.e. the polynomial with roots q_v^{n−1}λ_j^{−1}.

(3) is AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.7/dual-and-character-twist-hecke-comparison at rank n, which uses the same Hecke polynomial convention; uniqueness of the semisimple realization is Brauer–Nesbitt with Chebotarev.

(4): the condition λ_a/λ_b ∉ {1, q_v} for all ordered pairs a ≠ b is invariant under λ ↦ q_v^{n−1}λ^{−1}, which sends the ratio λ_a/λ_b to λ_b/λ_a; unramifiedness at 𝔭_i is unchanged by duals and cyclotomic twists at 𝔭_i ∤ ℓ.
The formalism of ι is the parent's IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.5/dual-hecke-ideal (stated there for the rank-2n quasi-split datum) and Tau Ceti's HeckeAntiInvolution.ofAmbient.

If ρ_𝔪 is decomposed generic at 𝔭_i then so is ρ_{𝔪^∨}.

nodes.title: Hecke-equivariant Poincaré duality on S_K and on Mantovan's Igusa varieties
nodes.statement: (1) Let d = dim S_K and Λ = ℤ/ℓ^r. The Poincaré pairing H^i(S_{K,Ē}, Λ) × H^{2d−i}(S_{K,Ē}, Λ(d)) → Λ of the smooth proper E-variety S_K is perfect, and the transpose of the action of t ∈ 𝕋^S is the action of ι(t). Hence for every maximal ideal 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^S, RΓ(S_{K,Ē}, Λ)_𝔪 ≅ RHom_Λ(RΓ(S_{K,Ē}, Λ)_{𝔪^∨}, Λ)[−2d](−d); in particular H^i(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0 for all i > d as soon as H^i(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_{𝔪^∨} = 0 for all i < d. The same holds for 𝔽_ℓ-local systems L on S_K attached to finite 𝔽_ℓ[K/K′]-modules, with L^∨ on the dual side. (2) Let p ∉ S ∪ {ℓ} be split in 𝒦, b ∈ B(G, μ^{−1}) and I^b_{Mant,m} Mantovan's Igusa variety of level m (smooth of dimension d_b = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ over 𝔽̄_p). For the Hecke operators at primes q ∉ S ∪ {p, ℓ}, which act through G(𝔸_f^p), RΓ_c(I^b_{Mant,m}, Λ)_{𝔪^∨} ≅ RHom_Λ(RΓ(I^b_{Mant,m}, Λ)_𝔪, Λ)[−2d_b](−d_b), compatibly with pullback along the finite étale transition maps on RΓ and trace on RΓ_c.
hypotheses: (1) K neat, S_K smooth proper of dimension d (IG.8 integral model, or directly over E).
(2) p ∉ S ∪ {ℓ} split in 𝒦; localization at maximal ideals of 𝕋^{S∪{p}}.
proofSteps: Perfectness of the pairing for smooth separated varieties with torsion coefficients: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2:pairings/poincare-duality-torsion (H_c = H for the proper S_K).

Hecke correspondences: a double coset [KgK] acts by the correspondence S_{K∩gKg^{−1}} ⇉ S_K (pullback then trace); its transpose under the cup-product pairing is the correspondence with the two maps exchanged, which is [Kg^{−1}K]; this is the étale form of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.5:finite-level-duality/hecke-adjoint-duality.
Localization: the pairing is 𝕋^S-equivariant for t on the left and ι(t) on the right, so the 𝔪-part pairs perfectly with the ι(𝔪)-part.

(2) is the parent's IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.5/igusa-poincare-duality, whose argument uses only that I^b_{Mant,m} is smooth of dimension d_b (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.1/mantovan-igusa-variety) and the away-from-p Hecke action; it applies verbatim to the unramified PEL data of this roadmap.
acceptance: For d = 0 (n = 1) the statement is the perfect pairing on functions on a finite set, with T and ι(T) transposes.
Taking Λ = 𝔽_ℓ: H^d(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0 iff H^d(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_{𝔪^∨} ≠ 0.

nodes.title: Caraiani–Scholze auxiliary primes for a residual representation
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(𝔽̄_ℓ) be a continuous semisimple representation unramified outside the places above S ∪ {ℓ}. A pair (p, 𝔭), with p ∈ Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) and 𝔭 | p a prime of the reflex field E (equivalently a compatible ι_p), is a CS-auxiliary pair for ρ̄ if for every prime 𝔭_i of F above u (p = uu^c) the set S_i contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0, and, if it contains one, ρ̄|_{Gal(F̄_{𝔭_i}/F_{𝔭_i})} is decomposed generic: unramified with Frobenius eigenvalues λ_1, …, λ_n satisfying λ_a/λ_b ∉ {1, q_{𝔭_i}} for all a ≠ b.
hypotheses: ρ̄ semisimple, unramified outside S ∪ {ℓ}; p ∈ Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}).
proofSteps: Decomposed genericity at a place is AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.7/strong-local-decomposed-genericity (Caraiani–Scholze's Definition 1.9 = 6.2.1 over an arbitrary finite extension of ℚ_p); the sets S_i are those of the split-prime decomposition.
The condition depends on the semisimplification only and is unchanged by replacing arithmetic by geometric Frobenius.
acceptance: If p splits completely in F and ρ̄ is unramified and decomposed generic at every place above p, (p, 𝔭) is CS-auxiliary for every 𝔭.

Defines decomposed genericity of an unramified mod-ℓ representation of a p-adic Galois group by λ_a/λ_b ∉ {1, q}.

nodes.title: Existence of auxiliary primes (Remarks 6.3.2–6.3.3, corrected)
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ be as in the auxiliary-prime condition. (a) If some rational prime p₀ ≠ ℓ splits completely in F and ρ̄ is unramified and decomposed generic at every place above p₀, then there are infinitely many such primes, they can be chosen outside any finite set (in particular outside S ∪ {ℓ}), and for each such p every (p, 𝔭) is a CS-auxiliary pair. (b) Suppose the signature of G is definite ((0, n) or (n, 0)) at all but one infinite place of F⁺ and ρ̄ is unramified and decomposed generic at some finite place v₀ of F. Then there are infinitely many places v of F of degree one over a rational prime p ∉ S ∪ {ℓ}, split in 𝒦, at which ρ̄ is unramified and decomposed generic; for such v, taking u the place of 𝒦 below v and choosing ι_p (hence 𝔭) so that ι_p^{−1} ∘ τ₀ induces v for the embedding τ₀ with p_{τ₀}q_{τ₀} ≠ 0 lying over u, (p, 𝔭) is a CS-auxiliary pair.
hypotheses: ρ̄ continuous semisimple, unramified outside a finite set.
(b): definite signature at all infinite places of F⁺ but one.
proofSteps: (a) Let L be the Galois closure over ℚ of the compositum of F, the field cut out by ρ̄ and ℚ(ζ_ℓ). The Frobenius class of p₀ in Gal(L/ℚ) is trivial on F and determines the eigenvalue ratios at all places above p₀ and p₀ mod ℓ; Chebotarev (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/haar-measure-chebotarev-clopen) gives a positive density of primes with the same class, each of which is again a witness; this is the argument of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.7/infinitely-many-decomposed-generic-primes with the strong condition λ_a/λ_b ∉ {1, q} in place of λ_a ≠ qλ_b.
Complete splitting puts p in Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} and makes every S_i a singleton, so the cardinality condition holds.

(b) Apply Chebotarev to Frob_{v₀} in Gal(L/F): only places of degree one contribute to the Dirichlet density (CS17 footnote 33), so there are infinitely many degree-one places v with the same Frobenius class, hence decomposed generic; the rational prime p below v splits in 𝒦 because v has degree one over p.

Corrected count (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E95): when the non-definite place of F⁺ is indefinite there are exactly two embeddings τ₀, τ₀c with p_τq_τ ≠ 0, one over u and one over u^c; only τ₀ lies in ⋃_i S_i, and choosing ι_p with ι_p^{−1}∘τ₀ inducing v puts it in S_i for 𝔭_i = v. If that place is also definite there is none and the condition holds trivially.
acceptance: For p splitting completely in F, the S_i are singletons.
In the Harris–Taylor case one decomposed-generic place suffices.

The main theorem assumes a completely decomposed prime with decomposed-generic ρ_𝔪; Remark 1.5 announces the weaker hypothesis for definite-but-one signatures.

nodes.title: Newton reduction kills generic principal series at a non-quasi-split factor (CS17 Lemma 5.4.3, corrected)
nodes.statement: In the split-prime decomposition at p, let π^n⃗_p = ⊗_{i=1}^m π^n⃗_{𝔭_i} ⊗ π^n⃗_0 ∈ Irr(G_n⃗(ℚ_p)), G_n⃗(ℚ_p) = ∏_i GL_n⃗(F_{𝔭_i}) × ℚ_p^×. Suppose some i satisfies: the transfer of π^n⃗_{𝔭_i} to GL_n(F_{𝔭_i}) along η̃_n⃗ (normalized induction twisted by the ϖ-character) is a generic principal series, and J_{b_i} is a non-quasi-split inner form of M_{b_i}. Then Red^b_n⃗(π^n⃗_p) = 0, where Red^b_n⃗ is the normalized Newton reduction including the modulus twist δ̄^{1/2}_{P(ν_b)}.
hypotheses: p split in 𝒦 and unramified in F; b = ((b_i), b_0) ∈ B(G, μ^{−1}).
Red^b_n⃗ the twisted reduction of ET.7b (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E74); the twist does not affect vanishing.
proofSteps: Red^b_n⃗ is the composite of normalized Jacquet functors to the effective endoscopic Levi subgroups, transfer along η̃_n⃗ to M_b (a normalized parabolic induction between products of general linear groups), and the Langlands–Jacquet map Groth(M_b(ℚ_p)) → Groth(J_b(ℚ_p)) (ET.7b/newton-reduction), all factoring over the 𝔭_i (split-prime decomposition).

If the transfer of π^n⃗_{𝔭_i} is a generic principal series, its Langlands parameter is a sum of characters with no ratio equal to |·|^{±1}; the L-morphism LM_{G_n⃗} → LM_b is the restriction of η̃_{n₁,n₂}, so every constituent of the image of π^n⃗_{𝔭_i} in Groth(M_{b_i}(F_{𝔭_i})) is a generic irreducible principal series (Jacquet modules of principal series: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.2/principal-series-jacquet).

The Langlands–Jacquet map of a non-quasi-split inner form kills every irreducible generic principal series: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6/principal-series-nontransfer (Badulescu); the J_{b_i}-factor of Red^b_n⃗(π^n⃗_p) is therefore zero, and so is the tensor product.
CS17 prints the conclusion as Red^b_n⃗(π_p) = 0; the representation is π^n⃗_p (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E75).
acceptance: For n = 2, b_i basic with J_{b_i} = D^× (quaternion) and π^n⃗_{𝔭_i} an unramified generic principal series, Red = 0; the trivial representation of GL_2 is not generic and its Langlands–Jacquet image is −1_{D^×} ≠ 0.

Defines the reduction as Jacquet functors, transfer along η̃_n⃗, and the Langlands–Jacquet map.

nodes.title: Spectral expansion of Igusa cohomology for the compact quasi-split datum (CS17 Lemma 5.5.1 and Corollary 5.5.2, corrected)
nodes.statement: In the Case 2 setting fix b, (f_n)^{S′} ∈ H^ur(𝒢_n(𝔸^{S′})), f_{n,S′_fin∖{p}} and their BC-transfers, and let φ_p ∈ C_c^∞(J_b(ℚ_p)) be arbitrary (not necessarily acceptable). (1) tr(φ | ι_ℓ[H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]) is a finite linear combination of products tr((Π^n⃗)^{S′}((f^n⃗)^{S′}) ∘ A^{S′}) · tr((Π^n⃗)_{S′_fin∖{p}}(f^n⃗_{S′_fin∖{p}}) ∘ A) · tr(Red^b_n⃗(π^n⃗_p)(φ_p)), where Π^n⃗ runs over θ-stable irreducible isobaric automorphic representations of 𝒢_n⃗ of the form n-Ind(Π_M)_ξ with Π_M in the discrete spectrum of a Levi M, Π^n⃗_∞ is cohomological for one of the coefficient systems Ξ(φ_n⃗) entering f^n⃗_∞ (trivial exactly when n⃗ = (n)), and π^n⃗_p ∈ Irr(G_n⃗(ℚ_p)) is the unique representation base-changing to Π^n⃗_p. (2) Fix φ_{S′_fin∖{p}} and φ_p and put Π^{S′} := ζ̃_{n⃗,*}(Π^n⃗)^{S′}. If the sum of the terms of (1) over all n⃗′ and Π^{n⃗′} with ζ̃_{n⃗′,*}(Π^{n⃗′})^{S′} ≅ Π^{S′} is a nonzero function of (f_n)^{S′}, then Π^{S′} occurs in BC^{S′}([H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]^{S′-ur}); conversely every irreducible 𝒢_n(𝔸^{S′})-subrepresentation of BC^{S′}([H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]^{S′-ur}) is of the form ζ̃_{n⃗,*}(Π^n⃗)^{S′}.
hypotheses: Case 2 datum of Layer IG.8 with p ∉ S split in 𝒦 and K_p hyperspecial; S′ := S ∪ {∞, p} ∪ Ram(ϖ) for a Hecke character ϖ : 𝔸_𝒦^×/𝒦^× → ℂ^× extending the quadratic character of 𝒦/ℚ and ramified only at primes of Spl_{F/F⁺}; ι_ℓ : ℚ̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ fixed.
Finite-level and infinity-type data fixed; finiteness is for fixed test functions, not uniform in the level.
proofSteps: For acceptable φ_p combine the stable Igusa trace identity with the spectral side of ET.4/twisted-spectral-side (Weyl-group denominator corrected, PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E71): a finite sum of tr(n-Ind(Π_M)_ξ(f^n⃗) ∘ A′).

Each n-Ind(Π_M)_ξ is irreducible and isobaric (ET.4/unitary-induction-irreducibility; Mœglin–Waldspurger classification ET.7a/residual-spectrum-classification), determined by its component outside S′ (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3/isobaric-strong-multiplicity-one).
Cohomological type at ∞: Π^n⃗_∞ is cohomological for Ξ(φ_n⃗), not for the trivial representation, when n⃗ is proper (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E77; ET.4/archimedean-lefschetz-functions).
At p: base change at the split prime p is injective, so tr(Π^n⃗_p(f^n⃗_p) ∘ A′_p) = ± tr π^n⃗_p(φ^n⃗_p), and Lemma 5.4.2 (ET.7b/red-trace-duality) rewrites it as tr Red^b_n⃗(π^n⃗_p)(φ_p).
Extension to all φ_p: the Frobenius-twist argument of [Shi09, Lemma 6.4] (ET.5/central-shift-character-separation; the printed reference is corrected in PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E78 and /E88).

(2): rewrite the (f^n⃗)^{S′} traces through ζ̃* (ET.4/unramified-transfers) and BC*, and apply linear independence of the finitely many distinct characters of the commutative unramified Hecke algebra occurring after fixing the test functions at the bad places (an elementary character-separation argument, valid in rank n); only the total coefficient of an eigensystem is detected (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E79), so the hypothesis of (2) is on that total.
acceptance: With φ_p = 0 every term vanishes.
Two terms with the same unramified eigensystem and coefficients 1 and −1 cancel; (2) then asserts nothing for that eigensystem.

sources.match: Writes the trace as a finite combination of products of traces of θ-stable isobaric Π^n⃗ away from S, at S_fin ∖ {p}, and of Red^b_n⃗(π^n⃗_p) at p; first for acceptable φ_p, then for all φ_p by the Frobenius-twist argument.
Relates contributing Π^n⃗ to subrepresentations of BC^S of the S-unramified Igusa class by linear independence of unramified Hecke characters; the remark notes that one Π^S may come from several n⃗.

nodes.title: The r-part of the base-changed Igusa class
nodes.statement: In the Case 2 setting, let r : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(ℚ̄_ℓ) be a continuous semisimple representation unramified outside the places above S′ ∪ {ℓ}. Write BC^{S′}([H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]^{S′-ur}) as a sum Σ_j n_j [Π_j^{S′} ⊗ σ_j] with Π_j^{S′} irreducible unramified representations of 𝒢_n(𝔸^{S′}) and σ_j irreducible representations of G(𝔸_{S′_fin∖{p}}) × J_b(ℚ_p). The r-part BC^{S′}([H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]^{S′-ur})_r is the sub-sum over the j with r_{Π_j^{S′},ℓ} ≅ r, where r_{Π^{S′},ℓ} is the Galois representation attached to Π^{S′} (CS17 Corollary 5.5.5, exported by AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.7/unitary-discrete-parameter-export).
hypotheses: Case 2 datum of Layer IG.8 with p ∉ S split in 𝒦 and K_p hyperspecial; S′ := S ∪ {∞, p} ∪ Ram(ϖ) for a Hecke character ϖ : 𝔸_𝒦^×/𝒦^× → ℂ^× extending the quadratic character of 𝒦/ℚ and ramified only at primes of Spl_{F/F⁺}; ι_ℓ : ℚ̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ fixed.
r semisimple; one base change BC^{S′} is used throughout (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E85).
proofSteps: Every Π_j^{S′} that occurs is ζ̃_{n⃗,*}(Π^n⃗)^{S′} by the converse part of the spectral expansion, so r_{Π_j^{S′},ℓ} is defined: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.2/cs-discrete-polarization-normalization and AG2.7/unitary-discrete-parameter-export give r_{Π^{S′},ℓ} = ⊕_i r_i ⊗ ε_i with the Hecke polynomials at the places above q ∈ Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S′ ∪ {ℓ}).
r_{Π^{S′},ℓ} depends only on Π^{S′} (Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt), so the sub-sum is well defined, and it is a summand of the Grothendieck-group element.
acceptance: The sum over all r of the r-parts is the whole class.
If no constituent has r_{Π^{S′},ℓ} ≅ r the r-part is 0.

sources.match: Fixes r unramified outside S ∪ {ℓ} and restricts attention to the summand of the base-changed S-unramified Igusa class coming from Π^S with r_{Π^S,ℓ} ≅ r (the printed BC^p is read as BC^S, PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E85).

uses.how: the vanishing statement is about this summand
a lift r of ρ_𝔪 with nonzero r-part is produced and Theorem 5.5.7 is applied to it

api.name: igusaGaloisPart
api.statement: BC^{S′}([H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]^{S′-ur})_r as an element of Groth(𝒢_n(𝔸^{S′}) × G(𝔸_{S′_fin∖{p}}) × J_b(ℚ_p)).

api.name: igusaGaloisPart_add
api.statement: The class is the (locally finite) sum of its r-parts over isomorphism classes of r.

api.name: igusaGaloisPart_eq_zero_of_not_occurs
api.statement: The r-part is zero iff no constituent Π^{S′} has r_{Π^{S′},ℓ} ≅ r.

api.name: igusaGaloisPart_iso
api.statement: The r-part depends only on the isomorphism class of r.

api.name: igusaGaloisPart_frobenius
api.statement: For a constituent of the r-part, the Satake parameters of Π^{S′} at v | q ∈ Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S′ ∪ {ℓ}) are the roots of the characteristic polynomial of r(Frob_v) (via ι_ℓ).

api.name: igusaGaloisPart.similitude_independent
api.statement: The r-index is determined by the normalized GL_n(𝔸_F)-component; two constituents differing only in the GL₁(𝔸_𝒦) similitude character have the same r-index.

tests.name: igusaGaloisPart_zero_class
tests.statement: For the zero class every r-part is zero.

tests.name: igusaGaloisPart_sum
tests.statement: Σ_r igusaGaloisPart r = BC^{S′}([H_c]^{S′-ur}) in the Grothendieck group, the sum being locally finite.

tests.name: igusaGaloisPart_not_bcp
tests.statement: Replacing BC^{S′} by a base change at the single place p (the printed BC^p) does not define a sub-sum indexed by Galois representations, since r_{Π,ℓ} depends on the component outside S′.

tests.name: igusaGaloisPart_n1
tests.statement: For n = 1, Π = ψ ⊗ Π⁰ has a GL₁(𝔸_𝒦) similitude factor ψ and a GL₁(𝔸_F) factor Π⁰. Distinct Π⁰-components outside S′ give distinct Galois characters (with the fixed normalization); changing only ψ while fixing Π⁰ leaves the r-index unchanged. Thus r-parts need not distinguish full automorphic characters of 𝒢₁.

nodes.title: A non-μ-ordinary class has a non-quasi-split factor at a nontrivial 𝔭_i
nodes.statement: In the split-prime decomposition at p, assume each S_i contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0. If b = ((b_i), b_0) ∈ B(G, μ^{−1}) is not μ-ordinary, then there is an index i such that S_i contains a τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0 and J_{b_i} is not quasi-split. Conversely the μ-ordinary class has every J_{b_i} quasi-split, J_{b_i} ≅ Res_{F_{𝔭_i}/ℚ_p}(GL_{p_τ} × GL_{q_τ}) at the nontrivial indices.
hypotheses: p ∉ S split in 𝒦; each S_i contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0.
proofSteps: B(G, μ^{−1}) = ∏_i B(G_i, μ_i^{−1}) and the maximal element is the product of the maximal elements (BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1/product-and-unramified-norm, BG1/ordinary-class).
If S_i contains no τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0, μ_i is central and B(G_i, μ_i^{−1}) is a point, the μ_i-ordinary one.

If S_i contains exactly one such τ, the corrected identification B(G_i, μ_i^{−1}) ≅ B(GL_n/F_{𝔭_i}, μ_{i,τ}^{−1}) of the split-prime decomposition (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E87) preserves J_b up to Res_{F_{𝔭_i}/ℚ_p} and the μ-ordinary class; by Lemma 5.5.8 (BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1/gl-minuscule-quasisplit-centralizer) only the μ-ordinary class has quasi-split J_b, and restriction of scalars preserves (non-)quasi-splitness.
If b is not μ-ordinary some factor b_i is not μ_i-ordinary; by the previous two steps that index has a nontrivial τ and a non-quasi-split J_{b_i}.
acceptance: For n = 2 and (p_τ, q_τ) = (1, 1): B(GL_2/F_{𝔭_i}, μ^{−1}) has two classes, the ordinary one (J = GL_1 × GL_1) and the basic one of slope −1/2 (J = D^×, non-quasi-split).

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.5.7, pp. 747–748, and Lemma 5.5.8, p. 748
sources.match: Shows that a non-μ-ordinary b has some i with a nontrivial τ in S_i and J_{b_i} not quasi-split, by decomposing B(G, μ^{−1}) as a product, treating central μ_i and reducing the single-τ case to Lemma 5.5.8 for GL_n over F_{𝔭_i}.

nodes.title: Genericity forces the μ-ordinary Newton stratum (CS17 Theorem 5.5.7)
nodes.statement: In the Case 2 setting fix ι_p compatible with the chosen 𝔭 | p of E and let r : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(ℚ̄_ℓ) be continuous semisimple, unramified outside the places above S′ ∪ {ℓ}. Assume (i) each S_i = {τ | ι_p^{−1}∘τ induces 𝔭_i} contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0, and (ii) for each i such that S_i contains such a τ, r|_{Gal(F̄_{𝔭_i}/F_{𝔭_i})} ≅ χ_{i,1} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_{i,n} with χ_{i,a}χ_{i,b}^{−1} not the cyclotomic character for all a ≠ b. Then for every b ∈ B(G, μ^{−1}) that is not μ-ordinary, BC^{S′}([H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]^{S′-ur})_r = 0.
hypotheses: Case 2 datum of Layer IG.8 with p ∉ S split in 𝒦 and K_p hyperspecial; S′ := S ∪ {∞, p} ∪ Ram(ϖ) for a Hecke character ϖ : 𝔸_𝒦^×/𝒦^× → ℂ^× extending the quadratic character of 𝒦/ℚ and ramified only at primes of Spl_{F/F⁺}; ι_ℓ : ℚ̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ fixed.
Hypotheses (i) and (ii) as stated; the sets S_i use ι_p^{−1}∘τ (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E86).
proofSteps: Suppose the r-part is nonzero for a non-μ-ordinary b. By the spectral expansion (2) there is a θ-stable isobaric Π^n⃗ whose total contribution is nonzero, with r_{ζ̃_*(Π^n⃗)^{S′},ℓ} ≅ r, and π^n⃗_p its base-change preimage.

Local–global compatibility at 𝔭_i (CS17 Remark 5.5.6, exported in AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.7/unitary-discrete-parameter-export with AG2.5/caraiani-upgrade-away-from-p-and-temperedness): hypothesis (ii) makes the transfer of π^n⃗_{𝔭_i} a generic principal series of GL_n(F_{𝔭_i}) at every nontrivial index i.
By the lemma on non-μ-ordinary classes there is a nontrivial index i with J_{b_i} not quasi-split; by the Newton reduction lemma Red^b_n⃗(π^n⃗_p) = 0.
So every term of the spectral expansion attached to such Π^n⃗ vanishes for every φ_p, contradicting the nonzero total contribution.
acceptance: If every S_i contains no τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0 (G_ℝ definite), B(G, μ^{−1}) is a point and the statement is empty.

Local rank-two check: at a split GL₂-factor with minuscule signature (1,1), the Newton set has an ordinary class and a basic class with non-quasi-split J_b. Keeping all other factors of an existing admissible Case 2 datum fixed, a generic r excludes this basic factor. This is a local calculation and asserts no existence of a global datum with arbitrarily prescribed signatures.

sources.match: States and proves that, under the condition on the sets S_i and the decomposition of r at the 𝔭_i into characters with non-cyclotomic ratios, the r-part of the base-changed Igusa class vanishes for non-μ-ordinary b, via Remark 5.5.6, Lemma 5.4.3, Lemma 5.5.1 and Lemma 5.5.8.

nodes.title: Igusa trace formula for Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties: only the stable term (CS17 Proposition 5.6.1)
nodes.statement: In the Case 1 setting, let b ∈ B(G, μ^{−1}) and φ = φ^pφ_p ∈ C_c^∞(G(𝔸_f^p) × J_b(ℚ_p)) with φ_p acceptable. Then tr(φ | ι_ℓ[H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]) = |ker¹(ℚ, G)| ι(G, G_n) ST^{G_n}_e(φ^{G_n}), where φ^{G_n} is Shin's endoscopic test function for the trivial endoscopic datum.
hypotheses: Case 1 datum of Layer IG.8 (B a central division algebra of degree n over F with an involution of the second kind, V ≅ B), p ∉ S split in 𝒦 (so B is split at every place of F above p and G(ℚ_p) ≅ ∏_i GL_n(F_{𝔭_i}) × ℚ_p^×), K_p hyperspecial, G_n the quasi-split inner form of G over ℚ with a fixed isomorphism G_n ≅ G over ℚ_p; ι_ℓ fixed.
φ_p acceptable.
proofSteps: Start from Shin's stable trace formula for Igusa varieties of PEL type (A): EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.5/stable-trace-with-normalizations, a sum over E_ell(G) = E_ell(G_n).

Vanishing of the proper terms ([Shi10, Lemma 7.1], cited by CS17): for a proper datum G_{n₁,n₂}, let d_v be the local index of B at a place v of F; since B has degree n and is a division algebra, lcm_v(d_v) = n, so some v has d_v ∤ n₁. At that place the local factor of G is GL_{n/d_v}(D_v) and that of H is GL_{n₁} × GL_{n₂}; an element of GL_n(F_v) that comes from GL_{n/d_v}(D_v) has characteristic polynomial whose irreducible factors all have degree divisible by d_v, which for the image of a (G, H)-regular γ_H would force d_v | n₁. So no such γ_H has an image (ET.0/norm-correspondence), the transfer of φ_v to H vanishes on all (G, H)-regular classes and ST^H_e(φ^H) = 0.
The surviving term is the trivial datum with coefficient ι(G, G_n) = τ(G)τ(G_n)^{−1}.
CS17 follows [Shi12, §6], which assumes p inert in F⁺; that assumption is not used.
acceptance: With φ_p = 0 both sides vanish.
For n = 1 there is no proper endoscopy and the identity is the trivial-datum case of Shin's formula.

sources.match: For the simple Shimura varieties with B split above p and acceptable φ_p, the Igusa trace equals |ker¹| ι(G, G_n) times the stable elliptic term for G_n; the other terms vanish by Shin's Lemma 7.1, and the inert hypothesis of [Shi12, §6] is not needed.

nodes.title: Newton reduction of the cohomology of the simple Shimura variety (stable Lefschetz identity)
nodes.statement: In the Case 1 setting put [H(Sh, ℚ̄_ℓ)] := Σ_i (−1)^i lim→_K H^i(S_{K,Ē}, ℚ̄_ℓ) ∈ Groth(G(𝔸_f)), and let Red^b_n : Groth(G(ℚ_p)) → Groth(J_b(ℚ_p)) be the Newton reduction for the trivial datum (normalized Jacquet functor, then the Langlands–Jacquet map, with the modulus twist), applied to the p-component through G(ℚ_p) ≅ G_n(ℚ_p). Then Red^b_n([H(Sh, ℚ̄_ℓ)]) = ε_G · d(G_ℝ) · [H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)] in Groth(G(𝔸_f^p) × J_b(ℚ_p)), with ε_G, d(G_ℝ) nonzero constants depending only on G.
hypotheses: Case 1 datum of Layer IG.8 (B a central division algebra of degree n over F with an involution of the second kind, V ≅ B), p ∉ S split in 𝒦 (so B is split at every place of F above p and G(ℚ_p) ≅ ∏_i GL_n(F_{𝔭_i}) × ℚ_p^×), K_p hyperspecial, G_n the quasi-split inner form of G over ℚ with a fixed isomorphism G_n ≅ G over ℚ_p; ι_ℓ fixed.
The constants are those produced by comparing the Euler–Poincaré function of G(ℝ) with Shin's archimedean test function for the trivial datum.
proofSteps: Since S_K is proper, H^*(S_{K,Ē}, ℚ̄_ℓ) ≅ H^*(S_K(ℂ), ℂ) through ι_ℓ and Artin's comparison (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison), Hecke-equivariantly.

Arthur's L²-Lefschetz formula, here for a compact quotient: for f ∈ C_c^∞(G(𝔸_f)), tr(f | [H(Sh)]) = Σ_{a∈ker¹(ℚ,G)} Σ_{π on G^{(a)}} m_a(π) tr π_f(f) ep(π_∞) = Σ_a I^{G^{(a)}}(f^{(a)} · f_EP^{(a)}) (AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.6/l2-lefschetz with AS.6/compact-trace-specialization and the Euler–Poincaré function AS.6/general-euler-poincare); the geometric side has only elliptic terms because f_EP is stable cuspidal. All terms use the fixed local identifications with G; stabilize this sum over the PEL components. Constants in the displayed identity refer to this PEL convention, as in CS17 §5.6, pp. 749–750.

Stabilize the elliptic terms (ET.4/elliptic-stabilization); the proper endoscopic terms vanish by the local-index argument of the simple Igusa trace identity, leaving ι(G, G_n) ST^{G_n}_e(f^{G_n}) ([Shi12, Prop. 6.3] as cited in CS17).

Take f = φ^p · f_p with f_p := φ^{G_n}_p transported to G(ℚ_p): by Lemma 5.4.2 (ET.7b/red-trace-duality) tr π_p(f_p) = tr Red^b_n(π_p)(φ_p). The archimedean test functions differ by the nonzero factor ε_G d(G_ℝ) (ET.4/archimedean-lefschetz-functions). Comparing with the simple Igusa trace identity gives the trace identity for acceptable φ_p.

Extend to all φ_p ∈ C_c^∞(J_b(ℚ_p)) by [Shi09, Lemma 6.4] (ET.5/central-shift-character-separation; the printed reference [Shi11] is corrected in PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E88), and conclude in the Grothendieck group by nondegeneracy of the trace pairing.
acceptance: For b basic in the Harris–Taylor case this specializes to the formula expressing the Igusa class of the basic stratum through the Jacquet–Langlands transfer of the global cohomology.

Applying the identity to the zero element is trivial; for the μ-ordinary b, Red^b_n is the normalized opposite Jacquet functor to M_b = J_b followed by the modulus twist δ̄_{P(ν_b)}^{1/2}; the twist is retained also in the μ-ordinary case.

sources.locator: §5.6, paragraph between Proposition 5.6.1 and Corollary 5.6.2, p. 749
sources.match: Combines Proposition 5.6.1 with the stable trace formula for S_K (Arthur's formula for Lefschetz numbers of Hecke operators, simplified as in Shin's Proposition 6.3 since G has no endoscopy) and Lemma 5.4.2 to get the Newton reduction of the cohomology of S_K equal to a nonzero constant times the Igusa class, first for acceptable φ_p and then for all φ_p.

nodes.title: Igusa cohomology of simple Shimura varieties in terms of automorphic representations (CS17 Corollary 5.6.2)
nodes.statement: In the Case 1 setting, in Groth(G(𝔸_f^p) × J_b(ℚ_p)), [ι_ℓH_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)] = (−1)^{q(G)} Σ_{π_f} c(π_f) [π_f^p] [Red^b_n(π_p)], the sum over the irreducible admissible π_f of G(𝔸_f) such that π_f ⊗ π_∞ is automorphic on some G^{(a)} for some π_∞ cohomological for the trivial representation, with c(π_f) := (−1)^{q(G)}(ε_G d(G_ℝ))^{−1} Σ_{a∈ker¹(ℚ,G)} Σ_{π_∞ on G^{(a)}} m_a(π_f ⊗ π_∞) ep(π_∞), where m_a is the automorphic multiplicity on the PEL component G^{(a)}, with finite parts transported to G by the fixed local identifications, ep(π_∞) = Σ_i (−1)^i dim H^i(𝔤, K_∞; π_∞) and q(G) = ½ dim G(ℝ)/K_∞A_{G,∞}^0. The sum is locally finite: for each compact open subgroup only finitely many terms have invariants.
hypotheses: Case 1 datum of Layer IG.8 (B a central division algebra of degree n over F with an involution of the second kind, V ≅ B), p ∉ S split in 𝒦 (so B is split at every place of F above p and G(ℚ_p) ≅ ∏_i GL_n(F_{𝔭_i}) × ℚ_p^×), K_p hyperspecial, G_n the quasi-split inner form of G over ℚ with a fixed isomorphism G_n ≅ G over ℚ_p; ι_ℓ fixed.
proofSteps: Apply Matsushima separately to each component Sh_{K^{(a)}}(G^{(a)}, X^{(a)}) of S_K: H^*(S_K(ℂ), ℂ) = ⊕_a ⊕_{π on G^{(a)}} m_a(π) π_f^K ⊗ H^*(𝔤, K_∞; π_∞) (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.5/automorphic-comparison and AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.4/compact-quotient-spectrum). Thus the coefficient of [π_f] in [H(Sh)] is Σ_a Σ_{π_∞} m_a(π_fπ_∞) ep(π_∞). One may replace the sum over a by |ker¹| times a single coefficient only after proving those coefficients agree.
Apply the stable Lefschetz identity and divide by ε_G d(G_ℝ); Red^b_n acts only on the p-component.
Only π_∞ with H^*(𝔤, K_∞; π_∞) ≠ 0 contribute, i.e. cohomological for the trivial representation.
acceptance: When every contributing π_∞ is a discrete series, ep(π_∞) = (−1)^{q(G)} and c(π_f) = (ε_G d(G_ℝ))^{−1} Σ_a Σ_{π_∞} m_a(π_f ⊗ π_∞), a multiple of the automorphic multiplicity.
One-dimensional automorphic representations (π_∞ trivial) contribute with ep(1) = Euler characteristic of the compact dual.

If ker¹ has two components with transported multiplicities m₁ and m₂, the coefficient uses m₁ + m₂; retaining only one component fails this test. If all component multiplicities coincide it becomes |ker¹| times the single-component coefficient.

Then there is an isobaric automorphic representation Π = ψ ⊗ Π⁰ of GL_1(𝔸_𝒦) × GL_n(𝔸_F), Π⁰ = Π_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ Π_r with Π_j discrete and conjugate self-dual, such that Π_v ≅ BC_v(π_v) for every finite place v ∉ S_π and for every v ∈ S_π split in 𝒦 at which B is split above v, and Π⁰_∞ has the infinitesimal character of the base change of the trivial representation. Consequently there is a continuous semisimple r_{π,ℓ} : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(ℚ̄_ℓ), unramified at every finite place of F above q ∉ S_π ∪ {ℓ}, including q not split in 𝒦, with the characteristic polynomial of r_{π,ℓ}(Frob_v) the image of P_v under the Satake parameters of π_v, and with WD(r_{π,ℓ}|_{Gal(F̄_w/F_w)})^{F-ss} ≅ ι_ℓ^{−1}rec(Π⁰_w|det|^{(1−n)/2}) at every place w ∤ ℓ of F above a prime split in 𝒦 at which B is split.

nodes.title: The r-part of the Igusa class of a simple Shimura variety
nodes.statement: In the Case 1 setting, let r : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(ℚ̄_ℓ) be continuous semisimple. The r-part [H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]_r is (−1)^{q(G)} Σ_{π_f : r_{π,ℓ} ≅ r} c(π_f)[π_f^p][Red^b_n(π_p)], the sub-sum of the formula for the Igusa class over the π_f whose attached Galois representation is isomorphic to r. It is well defined: r_{π,ℓ} depends only on the components of π_f at almost all places split in 𝒦.
hypotheses: Case 1 datum of Layer IG.8 (B a central division algebra of degree n over F with an involution of the second kind, V ≅ B), p ∉ S split in 𝒦 (so B is split at every place of F above p and G(ℚ_p) ≅ ∏_i GL_n(F_{𝔭_i}) × ℚ_p^×), K_p hyperspecial, G_n the quasi-split inner form of G over ℚ with a fixed isomorphism G_n ≅ G over ℚ_p; ι_ℓ fixed.
proofSteps: Use the expression of the Igusa class from the simple Igusa cohomology formula and the Galois representations of the previous node.
Two π_f with the same components outside a finite set have isomorphic r_{π,ℓ} (Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt), so the sub-sum is determined by the Grothendieck-group element and r.
acceptance: The Igusa class is the locally finite sum of its r-parts.

nodes.title: Contraction of a maximal ideal to the Hecke operators away from p
nodes.statement: Let S′ ⊇ S be finite with ℓ ∉ S′ ∖ S, 𝕋^{S′} ⊂ 𝕋^S the subalgebra generated by the spherical algebras at the primes of Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S′ ∪ {ℓ}), and 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^S a maximal ideal with finite residue field. Then 𝔪′ := 𝔪 ∩ 𝕋^{S′} is a maximal ideal of 𝕋^{S′}, and for every 𝕋^S-module M (such as H^i(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ) or the cohomology of Igusa varieties) M_𝔪 is a localization of M_{𝔪′}; hence M_{𝔪′} = 0 implies M_𝔪 = 0, and M_𝔪 ≠ 0 implies M_{𝔪′} ≠ 0. If M is finite over a finite ring, M_{𝔪′} = ⊕_{𝔐 ∩ 𝕋^{S′} = 𝔪′} M_𝔐.
hypotheses: 𝔪 maximal with finite residue field (true for the support of H^*(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)).
proofSteps: 𝕋^{S′} → 𝕋^S/𝔪 has image a subring of a finite field, hence a field, so 𝔪′ is maximal.
Elements of 𝕋^{S′} ∖ 𝔪′ lie outside 𝔪, so localizing at 𝔪 factors through localizing at 𝔪′.
For M finite over a finite ring, M is a finite module over the Artinian image of 𝕋^S and splits as the sum of its localizations at the maximal ideals.

Used with S′ = S ∪ {p} (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E97).

nodes.title: Hochschild–Serre between finite level and the perfectoid Shimura variety
nodes.statement: Let 𝒮_{K^p} ∼ lim←_{K′_p} 𝒮_{K^pK′_p} be the perfectoid Shimura variety over C at infinite level at p and H^b(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ) = lim→_{K′_p} H^b(S_{K^pK′_p}, 𝔽_ℓ). There is a convergent spectral sequence E_2^{a,b} = H^a_cts(K_p, H^b(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ)) ⇒ H^{a+b}(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ), equivariant for 𝕋^{S∪{p}}. Consequently, for a maximal ideal 𝔪 of 𝕋^{S∪{p}}: (a) if H^i(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0 then H^j(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for some j ≤ i, in particular RΓ(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0; (b) if H^b(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0 for all b < d then H^i(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0 for all i < d.

K^p sufficiently small for the perfectoid tower; localization at 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^{S∪{p}}.
proofSteps: The perfectoid representative 𝒮_{K^p} of the Hodge-type tower (a PEL datum of type A is of Hodge type): PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S2/hodge-open-perfectoid-tower; continuity of étale cohomology along the tower: DiamondEtaleCohomology:C0/etale-cohomology-continuity.
Algebraic and analytic étale cohomology of the proper varieties S_{K^pK′_p} agree (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H5/proper-comparison-3-7-2).

𝒮_{K^p} → 𝒮_K is a pro-finite-étale K_p-torsor; the Cartan–Leray spectral sequence with continuous-cohomology E_2 for étale coefficients is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cartan-leray-spectral-sequence (b) (equivalently the colimit of the finite Hochschild–Serre sequences of SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/hochschild-serre-galois-covering).
Hecke operators at q ∉ S ∪ {p, ℓ} commute with the K_p-action, so the spectral sequence is 𝕋^{S∪{p}}-equivariant and localization (exact) can be applied termwise.

(a): if j₀ is the least degree with H^{j₀}(𝒮_{K^p})_𝔪 ≠ 0 then E_2^{a,b}_𝔪 = 0 for b < j₀, so H^i(S_K)_𝔪 = 0 for i < j₀. nodes.title: Reduction of perfectoid-level cohomology to Igusa cohomology through π_HT
nodes.statement: Let π_HT : 𝒮_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G,μ} be the Hodge–Tate period map and 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^{S∪{p}} maximal. Then Rπ_HT*𝔽_ℓ is a complex of sheaves of 𝕋^{S∪{p}}-modules, and for every geometric point x̄ of Fℓ^b_{G,μ}, ((Rπ_HT*𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪)_x̄ ≅ RΓ(Ig^b, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪. Consequently: (a) if RΓ(Ig^b, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0 for every b ∈ B(G, μ^{−1}), then RΓ(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0; (b) if H^i(Ig^b, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0 for all i < d and all b, then H^i(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0 for all i < d.
hypotheses: Compact unitary datum (Case 1 or 2) of Layer IG.8 with S, K = K_SK^S, ℓ a prime and 𝕋^S its Hecke algebra; p a prime in Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) with K = K_pK^p, K_p hyperspecial; all cohomology is étale cohomology after base change to an algebraically closed field (C = ℂ_p for the adic spaces).
Compact PEL datum of type (A) with good reduction at p (Layer IG.8 integral model).
proofSteps: The Hodge–Tate period map for Hodge type: PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S3/hodge-open-period-map; the Hecke operators away from p act trivially on Fℓ_{G,μ}, so the pushforward is a sheaf of 𝕋^{S∪{p}}-modules and localization commutes with stalks, and with cohomology on the quasi-compact, quasi-separated locally noetherian analytic flag variety by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-sheaf-colimit-of-constructible. The bounded-below pushforward and finite torsion cohomological dimension permit the corresponding derived localization.
Stalks: the compact fibre theorem IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.3/compact-fibre-theorem (CS17 Theorem 4.4.4), Hecke-equivariantly, for the proper integral model of Layer IG.8.
Stalks at all geometric points (including higher-rank points) are controlled by rank-one points (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.3/rank-one-cohomology-lemma); the strata Fℓ^b cover Fℓ_{G,μ}.

Leray: RΓ(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 = RΓ(Fℓ_{G,μ}, (Rπ_HT*𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪) (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7/grothendieck-spectral-sequence on the étale sites of DiamondEtaleCohomology:C0/etale-site); if all stalks vanish the complex is zero, and if all stalks lie in degrees ≥ d so does the complex and its hypercohomology.

For general restriction-of-scalars factors the flags use the corresponding local field; the statement does not identify all ordinary strata with ℚ_p-rational flags.

nodes.title: From the minimal Newton stratum to a nonzero dual Galois summand
nodes.statement: Let 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^{S∪{p}} be maximal and b ∈ B(G, μ^{−1}) with d_b = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ minimal among the classes with RΓ(Ig^b, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0. Then: (1) H^i(Ig^b, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0 only for i = d_b; for every Mantovan level m large enough the finite-level H^i(I^b_{Mant,m}, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 is nonzero exactly for i = d_b; (2) H^*(I^b_{Mant,m}, ℤ_ℓ)_𝔪 is free over ℤ_ℓ and concentrated in degree d_b, and H^*_c(I^b_{Mant,m}, ℤ_ℓ)_{𝔪^∨} is free and concentrated in degree d_b, nonzero; (3) the 𝔪^∨-part of [H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]^{S′-ur} (obtained by first selecting eigenvalues reducing to 𝔪^∨, then restricting to the operators away from S′_fin ∪ {ℓ}) is a nonzero element of the Grothendieck group; (4) there is a constituent whose unramified component Π^{S′} (Case 2: an irreducible subrepresentation of BC^{S′}([H_c(I^b_Mant, ℚ̄_ℓ)]^{S′-ur}); Case 1: π_f^{S′} for π_f in the simple Igusa cohomology formula) has Hecke eigenvalues lifting 𝔪^∨ ∩ 𝕋^{S′_fin}, and the r-part of the Igusa class for r = r_{Π^{S′},ℓ} (resp. r_{π,ℓ}) is nonzero.
hypotheses: Compact unitary datum (Case 1 or 2) of Layer IG.8 with S, K = K_SK^S, ℓ a prime and 𝕋^S its Hecke algebra; p a prime in Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) with K = K_pK^p, K_p hyperspecial; all cohomology is étale cohomology after base change to an algebraically closed field (C = ℂ_p for the adic spaces).
Localization at 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^{S∪{p}} (contracted ideal).
S′ = S ∪ {∞, p} ∪ Ram(ϖ) in Case 2.
proofSteps: (1): compact minimal-stratum concentration IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.4/compact-minimal-stratum-concentration (CS17 Corollary 6.1.4) with S ∪ {p} in place of S and the subalgebra 𝕋^{S∪{p}}; m-torsion and m-localization vanish together since H^i(Ig^b) = lim→ H^i(I^b_{Mant,m}) with split injective transition maps. Taking invariants under a pro-p compact open of J_b(ℚ_p) is exact on 𝔽_ℓ-modules (ℓ ≠ p), giving the finite-level statement (IG.1/perfection-of-mantovan, IG.1/igusa-group-actions).

(2): a bounded complex of finite ℤ_ℓ-modules whose reduction mod ℓ is concentrated in one degree has free cohomology in that degree only (universal coefficients and Nakayama). Hecke-equivariant Poincaré duality on I^b_{Mant,m} (Layer IG.8) turns this into the statement for H_c at 𝔪^∨.

(3): after ⊗ℚ̄_ℓ the 𝔪^∨-part of H_c^* is concentrated in degree d_b and nonzero, so no cancellation occurs in the alternating sum; the S′-unramified part keeps it since the level outside S′ is hyperspecial.

(4): Case 2: by the spectral expansion (Layer IG.9) and its part (2), some Π^{S′} occurs in BC^{S′} with nonzero total contribution; its Hecke eigenvalues lie in a finite extension and reduce to 𝔪^∨ by the Deligne–Serre lemma (AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.5/deligne-serre-eigenvalue-lifting-lemma) applied to the finite free ℤ_ℓ-lattice H^{d_b}_c(I^b_{Mant,m}, ℤ_ℓ)_{𝔪^∨}. Case 1: the same with the simple Igusa cohomology formula. The printed 'Theorem 5.5.5' is Corollary 5.5.5 (PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E99); the dual ideal enters through PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E98. Deligne–Serre gives a lift before forgetting operators at Ram(ϖ), but Π^{S′} remembers only the contraction to 𝕋^{S′_fin}. The polynomial comparison for its Galois representation is therefore claimed only outside S′_fin ∪ {ℓ}.

For n = 1, every b is μ-ordinary and the statement is about the cohomology of a finite set.

nodes.title: Galois representations for torsion Hecke eigensystems (CS17 Theorem 6.3.1(1))

There is a unique continuous semisimple ρ_𝔪 : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(𝔽̄_ℓ), unramified outside the places above S ∪ {ℓ}, such that for every finite place v of F above q ∈ Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) the characteristic polynomial of ρ_𝔪(Frob_v) is the image of P_v(X) = Σ_i (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2} T_{i,v} X^{n−i} under a fixed embedding 𝕋^S/𝔪 ↪ 𝔽̄_ℓ.

The auxiliary-character finite-avoidance input requested from ET.0 is an open prerequisite in Case 2. Case 1 also depends on the recorded AG2.2 gap. The unconditional source theorem is the target; this packet does not claim its prerequisite chains are closed.
proofSteps: Choose p ∈ Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) and contract 𝔪 to 𝔪′ ⊂ 𝕋^{S∪{p}} (hecke-contraction). By Hecke-equivariant Poincaré duality on S_K, H^*(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_{𝔪^∨} ≠ 0 too.
Hochschild–Serre (perfectoid-hochschild-serre (a)) gives RΓ(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ)_{𝔪′} ≠ 0, so by the Leray reduction some RΓ(Ig^b, 𝔽_ℓ)_{𝔪′} ≠ 0; take b with d_b minimal.

In Case 2 choose the auxiliary character ϖ and set S′ = S ∪ {p,∞} ∪ Ram(ϖ). The minimal-stratum node gives a constituent Π^{S′} lifting (𝔪′)^∨ ∩ 𝕋^{S′_fin}. AG2.7/unitary-discrete-parameter-export and AG2.7/residual-representation-of-pi give a residual representation unramified outside S′_fin ∪ {ℓ}, with the required polynomials at v above Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S′_fin ∪ {ℓ}). Dualize and twist by dual-hecke-ideal. In Case 1 use the requested simple-base-change-galois with the bad set S ∪ {p}. Do not discard Ram(ϖ) from the Case 2 comparison.

Uniqueness: two semisimple representations with the same Frobenius characteristic polynomials on a density-one set of places are isomorphic (Chebotarev ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5/haar-measure-chebotarev-clopen and Brauer–Nesbitt R01.1/brauer-nesbitt).

To remove every extra bad prime, fix an arbitrary rational q ∉ S ∪ {ℓ}. Choose p ≠ q, and in Case 2 choose ϖ unramified above q using the finite-avoidance request to ET.0. This gives a construction unramified at all places of F above q, and, when q splits in 𝒦, the desired polynomial there. All constructions agree by uniqueness on their common density-one set. Varying q proves unramifiedness outside S ∪ {ℓ} and all the stated polynomials. Merely choosing two p removes those auxiliary primes but does not by itself remove Ram(ϖ). This strengthens the use of the two-prime observation E97; the finite-avoidance step is recorded as a gap rather than assumed proved.
acceptance: For n = 1, ρ_𝔪 is the reduction of the Galois character attached by class field theory to the Hecke character of G.

Bad-set check: if q lies in Ram(ϖ) but not in S ∪ {p,ℓ}, one construction supplies no unramifiedness at q. A second construction must avoid q in both its auxiliary prime and its character ramification before uniqueness can remove q.

nodes.title: Middle-degree concentration of the generic part (CS17 Theorem 6.3.1(2))
nodes.statement: Let 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^S be a maximal ideal with H^*(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0 and ρ_𝔪 as above. Suppose there is a CS-auxiliary pair (p, 𝔭) for ρ_𝔪 (Layer IG.8): p ∈ Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) and a prime 𝔭 | p of E such that each S_i contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0 and ρ_𝔪 is decomposed generic at 𝔭_i whenever S_i contains such a τ. Then H^j(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0 only for j = d = dim S_K.
hypotheses: Compact unitary datum (Case 1 or 2) of Layer IG.8 with S, K = K_SK^S, ℓ a prime and 𝕋^S its Hecke algebra; p a prime in Spl_{𝒦/ℚ} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) with K = K_pK^p, K_p hyperspecial; all cohomology is étale cohomology after base change to an algebraically closed field (C = ℂ_p for the adic spaces).
Case 1 or Case 2; (p, 𝔭) a CS-auxiliary pair for ρ_𝔪.
proofSteps: By Hecke-equivariant Poincaré duality on S_K and the dual-ideal node (𝔪^∨ has a CS-auxiliary pair whenever 𝔪 does), it suffices to prove H^i(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0 for i < d for every such 𝔪; contract to 𝔪′ ⊂ 𝕋^{S∪{p}}.
By Hochschild–Serre (b) it suffices to show H^i(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ)_{𝔪′} = 0 for i < d.

Let b have d_b minimal with RΓ(Ig^b)_{𝔪′} ≠ 0. The minimal-stratum node gives a Galois representation r (attached to the constituent it produces) with nonzero r-part of the Igusa class of b; by part (1) and Chebotarev with Brauer–Nesbitt its semisimplified reduction is ρ_{𝔪^∨} = ρ_𝔪^∨ ⊗ ε̄^{1−n}, globally and hence at every 𝔭_i.

At each nontrivial 𝔭_i, ρ_{(𝔪′)^∨} is decomposed generic, so by CS17 Lemma 6.2.2 (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.5/generic-lift-splits, over the finite extension F_{𝔭_i} of ℚ_p) r|_{Gal(F̄_{𝔭_i}/F_{𝔭_i})} is a sum of characters with non-cyclotomic ratios. Theorem 5.5.7 (Case 2) or Corollary 5.6.3 (Case 1) forces b to be μ-ordinary, so d_b = ⟨2ρ, μ⟩ = d.

Since ⟨2ρ, ν_{b′}⟩ ≤ ⟨2ρ, μ⟩ = d with equality only for the μ-ordinary class, minimality forces every b′ with RΓ(Ig^{b′})_{𝔪′} ≠ 0 to be μ-ordinary; its cohomology is concentrated in degree d by minimal-stratum concentration. So H^i(Ig^{b′}, 𝔽_ℓ)_{𝔪′} = 0 for i < d and all b′, and the Leray reduction (b) gives H^i(𝒮_{K^p}, 𝔽_ℓ)_{𝔪′} = 0 for i < d.
acceptance: Concentration fails without localization: H^0(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ) ≠ 0 always (CS17 Remark 1.7).
For d = 0 the statement is that all localized cohomology is in degree 0.

sources.match: Under the auxiliary-prime condition, the localized cohomology is concentrated in degree dim S_K: reduce by Poincaré duality to the lower bound, pass to infinite level by Hochschild–Serre, take a minimal stratum, use Lemma 6.2.2 and Theorem 5.5.7 (or Corollary 5.6.3) to see that it is μ-ordinary, then conclude by Corollary 6.1.4, Theorem 4.4.4 and the Leray spectral sequence.
A characteristic-zero lift of a decomposed-generic unramified representation is a sum of characters with non-cyclotomic ratios and corresponds to a generic principal series.

nodes.title: Caraiani–Scholze's theorem for compact unitary Shimura varieties (CS17 Theorem 1.1)
nodes.statement: Let (G, X) be a compact unitary datum (Case 1 or 2), K = K_SK^S neat as in Layer IG.8, and 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^S a maximal ideal with H^i(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0. (1) There is an associated ρ_𝔪 : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(𝔽̄_ℓ). (2) If some rational prime p ≠ ℓ splits completely in F and ρ_𝔪 is unramified and decomposed generic at every place of F above p, then i = d. (3) If G_ℝ is definite at all infinite places of F⁺ but one and ρ_𝔪 is unramified and decomposed generic at some finite place of F, then i = d. In both (2) and (3) H^*(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 is concentrated in degree d. CS17 states Theorem 1.1 for the locally symmetric spaces X_Γ = Γ\X and gives its precise form as Theorem 6.3.1 for S_K(ℂ) = ⊔_j Γ_j\X; the statement here is that precise form.
hypotheses: Case 1 or Case 2; K neat with K^S hyperspecial (in Case 2, S ⊂ Spl_{F/F⁺}, so the level is hyperspecial at every prime outside Spl_{F/F⁺}).
proofSteps: (1) is torsion-galois-representations.
(2): by auxiliary-prime-existence (a) there is such p outside S ∪ {ℓ}, and every (p, 𝔭) is a CS-auxiliary pair; apply middle-degree-concentration.
(3): auxiliary-prime-existence (b) produces a CS-auxiliary pair (corrected Remark 6.3.3, PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17/E95); apply middle-degree-concentration.

The comparison with the locally symmetric spaces of the introduction is S_K(ℂ) = ⊔_j Γ_j\X with Γ_j = G^{(i)}(ℚ) ∩ g_jKg_j^{−1} (PELModuli:M3/complex-points); no statement about the localized cohomology of a single component is made.
acceptance: n = 1: d = 0 and the statement is trivially true.
Harris–Taylor signature: (3) needs only one decomposed-generic place (CS17 Remark 1.5).

sources.locator: §1, Theorem 1.1 with footnote 2, p. 651; Remarks 1.2–1.5, pp. 651–652
sources.match: Main theorem: Galois representations for systems of Hecke eigenvalues in the mod-ℓ cohomology of compact unitary locally symmetric spaces of Kottwitz's simple type (and the quasi-split case of footnote 2), and concentration in the middle degree when ρ_𝔪 is unramified and decomposed generic above a completely decomposed prime; Remark 1.5 weakens the hypothesis for definite-but-one signatures.
Explain how the conditions of the introduction give the hypothesis of Theorem 6.3.1(2).

nodes.title: Integral coefficients and twisted coefficient systems (CS17 Remarks 1.3 and 1.7.1)
nodes.statement: Let 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^S satisfy the conclusion of middle-degree concentration: H^i(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0 for i ≠ d. (1) Then H^i(S_K, ℤ_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0 for i ≠ d and H^d(S_K, ℤ_ℓ)_𝔪 is a free ℤ_ℓ-module. (2) Let K′ ⊂ K be a normal compact open subgroup with K′_q = K_q for q ∉ S′ (S′ ⊇ S finite), V a finite 𝔽_ℓ[K/K′]-module and L_V the associated local system on S_K. Let 𝔪 ⊂ 𝕋^{S′} be maximal and suppose that, if H^*(S_{K′}, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0, the representation ρ_𝔪 attached at level K′ (Galois representations for torsion eigensystems with S′ in place of S) admits a CS-auxiliary pair. Then H^i(S_K, L_V)_𝔪 ≠ 0 only for i = d. (3) For an irreducible algebraic representation ξ of G over a finite extension E_λ/ℚ_ℓ with a K-stable O_λ-lattice, the same holds for the ℤ_ℓ-local system L_ξ under the hypothesis of (2) at a normal compact open K′ ⊂ K on which L_ξ ⊗ 𝔽_ℓ becomes constant: H^i(S_K, L_ξ)_𝔪 = 0 for i ≠ d and H^d(S_K, L_ξ)_𝔪 is free over O_λ. In (2)–(3) K′ is required to be an admissible level for the constant-coefficient theorem; in Case 2 S′ ⊂ Spl_{F/F⁺}. The coefficient variant here is conditional on the existence of this level and does not claim to cover every ξ of Remark 1.7.1.
hypotheses: Compact unitary datum (Case 1 or 2) of Layer IG.8 with S, K = K_SK^S, ℓ a prime and 𝕋^S its Hecke algebra; all cohomology is étale cohomology after base change to an algebraically closed field (C = ℂ_p for the adic spaces).
(2)–(3): Hecke operators only at primes where K′ = K.

(2)–(3): the datum and level K′ must still satisfy all hypotheses of the constant-coefficient theorem with S′ replacing S; in Case 2 this requires S′ ⊂ Spl_{F/F⁺}. For (3) existence of such a trivializing level is an explicit hypothesis, not an assertion for every algebraic ξ.
proofSteps: (1): RΓ(S_K, ℤ_ℓ)_𝔪 is a perfect complex of ℤ_ℓ-modules with RΓ(S_K, ℤ_ℓ)_𝔪 ⊗^L 𝔽_ℓ = RΓ(S_K, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 concentrated in degree d; the universal coefficient sequences 0 → H^i(ℤ_ℓ)_𝔪/ℓ → H^i(𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 → H^{i+1}(ℤ_ℓ)_𝔪[ℓ] → 0 and Nakayama give vanishing for i ≠ d and torsion-freeness in degree d.

(2): the finite Galois cover S_{K′} → S_K with group K/K′ trivializes L_V; the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/hochschild-serre-galois-covering) E_2^{a,b} = H^a(K/K′, H^b(S_{K′}, 𝔽_ℓ) ⊗ V) ⇒ H^{a+b}(S_K, L_V) is 𝕋^{S′}-equivariant. Localized at 𝔪, the E_2 page vanishes outside the row b = d by middle-degree concentration at level K′ (and vanishes entirely if H^*(S_{K′}, 𝔽_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0), so H^i(S_K, L_V)_𝔪 = 0 for i < d.

Upper bound: Poincaré duality with local-system coefficients (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2:pairings/poincare-duality-torsion for locally constant constructible sheaves) identifies H^i(S_K, L_V)_𝔪 with the dual of H^{2d−i}(S_K, L_{V^∨}(d))_{𝔪^∨}, which vanishes for 2d − i < d by the lower bound for V^∨ and 𝔪^∨. The dual-ideal and auxiliary-pair nodes give the same genericity hypothesis for 𝔪^∨ at the same admissible level K′, so the lower bound really applies to the dual coefficients.
(3): apply (1)–(2) to L_ξ/ℓ (a local system attached to a finite 𝔽_ℓ[K/K′]-module) and pass to ℤ_ℓ by (1).
acceptance: For V = 𝔽_ℓ (trivial module, K′ = K), (2) is middle-degree concentration itself.
Without localization, H⁰(S_K,L_V) = (H⁰(S_{K′},𝔽_ℓ) ⊗ V)^{K/K′}; the action on components cannot be ignored. For trivial V this can be nonzero.
